questions.q: Which earlier chapter's templating pattern did Lesson 30's Helm chart actually apply?
questions.explain: helm create, a templated values.yaml, and two differently sized releases are Chapter 6's templating lesson, applied to a real app.

questions.q: Why did the Ingress in Lesson 30 need no re-explanation of what a Service does?
options: Services were introduced for the first time in this capstone
Because Chapter 4 already explained the ClusterIP/Service model before the Ingress lesson built on top of it
Ingress objects do not actually depend on Services at all
Because Chapter 7's security content covers networking as well
questions.explain: Chapter 4's networking content already established the Service model; the Ingress lab in Lesson 30 built on it rather than re-deriving it.

questions.q: Which chapter's ideas does Lesson 31's outage have to be read through -- QoS classes, OOMKilled vs. Evicted, and LimitRange?
questions.explain: Chapter 7 introduced the resource-governance and hardening ideas that Lesson 31's incident shows causing a real outage.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the next course after this one in the Cloud Engineer -> Cloud Architect path?
questions.explain: This course closes; the Advanced Specialization stage continues next with Cloud Reliability, Monitoring & FinOps.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real job this capstone proved, beyond getting a Deployment to reach Running?
options: Memorizing every kubectl subcommand that exists
Avoiding Helm entirely in favor of hand-applied YAML
Choosing a different base image for every container regardless of need
Understanding every object around a deployed application well enough to explain why a neighbor's mistake became everyone's incident
questions.explain: The capstone's real lesson is understanding the whole platform around a workload, not just getting one object to a healthy status.
